Subject: Kek wrapping & HSM proxy handshake — connectivity and rotation plan

Alex / Morgan team —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our onboarding checklist for Acme's private VPC deployment, we want to lock down the plan for: (1) the KEK wrapping/proxy handshake between your HSM cluster and Redwood's inference nodes, (2) operator separation for BYOK, and (3) a rotation cadence that satisfies Acme's audit team.

Attached is the first-pass network diagram (network_diagram_v1.pdf) and a short writeup of the proposed KEK flow (kek_handshake_flow.md). High-level asks from our side: 
- Confirm whether your HSM cluster will accept an outbound mutual-TLS connection to a dedicated HSM proxy (we would prefer no inbound firewall holes into your HSM subnet).
- Confirm the ephemeral port range you allow for control-plane heartbeats and attestation (we propose 49152-49170).
- Confirm operator split: Acme retains custodial key material (KEY_OWNER role), Redwood will hold the wrapped model keys only (SERVE role). We need to confirm who holds the split shares for emergency unseal.
- Confirm acceptable rotation window: quarterly vs. 30-day for KEK rewrap on production critical keys.

Next steps I propose: internal tech sync (Redwood infra + security) then a joint acceptance call with your ops team on Thu. Can folks confirm availability?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Naomi —

Appreciate the notes and attachments. A few quick clarifications from Acme Ops and Security: 
- Our HSM cluster is in a restricted subnet — we do not allow inbound connections from external IPs. We can initiate an outbound mTLS session to an approved Redwood HSM-proxy endpoint provided the proxy is hosted inside our VPC peering boundary (or via a managed cross-account endpoint with strict IAM). We need the proxy cert chain in advance for allowlisting.
- Port range 49152-49170 is acceptable for control-plane heartbeats; we also need a TLS-based health-check endpoint on 8443 for attestation callbacks.
- Regarding operator split: Acme requires at least 2-of-3 custodial quorum for emergency unseal, and any operator rekeying events must be logged to our SIEM (we'll provide a SQS/forwarder endpoint).
- Rotation cadence: Security prefers 90-day KEK rewrap for production model keys, but can make exceptions to 60 days for keys serving PII.

We are available Thu 2026-10-01 09:00-11:00 PT for the joint acceptance call. Can you send a calendar invite with dial-in + Zoom?

Best,
Alex Rivera
Senior Cloud Ops Engineer, Acme Corp
alex.rivera@acme-corp.com

Thanks — short technical notes ahead of the Thu call. I put the checklist items we should confirm in the meeting so we can get sign-off quickly.

1) Connectivity model (preferred):
   - Redwood deploys an HSM-proxy container in the Acme VPC (customer-managed subnet) and establishes VPC peering to Redwood inference subnets. Proxy initiates mTLS outbound to Acme HSMs for attestation and wrap operations. No inbound holes into HSM subnet.
   - Peer CIDR and security group: we will use a dedicated /28 for the proxy nodes; provide us with the allowlist cert fingerprint and proxy FQDN.

2) Ports & protocols:
   - Control-plane (attest/heartbeat): TCP 49152-49170, mutual TLS.
   - Attestation callback/health: TCP 8443 (HTTPS) with client cert verification.
   - Key wrap API: gRPC over TLS, port 10000 (internal, proxied).

3) KEK wrapping & operator split:
   - Flow: Acme master KEK (HSM-wrapped) -> Redwood receives WRAPPED_KEK blob via proxy -> Redwood stores wrapped form only; to unwrap for emergency, a 2-of-3 Acme operator quorum + Redwood support ticket required.
   - We propose automated rewrap job with one-time-use ephemeral session keys; rewrap initiated by Acme CI pipeline (signed request).

4) Rotation windows and audit:
   - Default: 90-day KEK rewrap for production; 60-day for PII-scoped keys.
   - Every rotation emits a signed rotation event to Acme's SIEM endpoint and Redwood's audit log. We will provide an audit bundle (signed JSON) per rotation.

5) Failover and emergency unseal:
   - If Acme operator quorum is unreachable, we will fall back to the documented emergency process: timed approval by two Acme execs + on-call Redwood security rotation to perform a temporary wrap-release. This will be treated as an exception and recorded.

Attachments: I uploaded a concise HSM acceptance checklist (hsm-attestation-checklist.xlsx) and a one-page KEK flow summary (kek_handshake_flow.md). Please review before Thu so we keep the call to 30 minutes.

- Aditya
